newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA C.BANK RESERVES DIP TO $697.7 MLN IN FEB.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA C.BANK RESERVES DIP TO $697.7 MLN IN FEB.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Wednesday its total foreign exchange reserves fell to $697.7 million in February from $812.2 million at end-January.
Central bank officials told Reuters the slide was triggered by external payments to service the country's foreign debt, which latest data put at $6.9 billion at end-1996.
Last week, foreign exchange dealers reported that the BNR had sold dollars on the market to prop up the leu currency. The BNR said it had only tested the market, declining to elaborate.
Since then, the leu firmed sharply, trading now near 6,000 to the dollar against about 9,000 earlier last week.
BNR data also showed foreign reserve assets in the banking system fell to $2.77 billion in January from $3.14 billion at end-1996. Data on February reserve assets were not available.
End-January reserve assets include gold reserves of about 88 tonnes, Special Drawing Rights and hard currency reserves of local banks and of the BNR.

On Tuesday, the lower chamber of parliament set the ceiling of Romania's 1997 foreign debt at $3.2 billion under a bill entitling the BNR and the finance ministry to raise and guarantee medium- and long-term loans from world markets to prop up reforms and enhance hard currency reserves.
In order to become effective the bill has to clear parliament's upper house, where Romania's centrist coalition government also relies on a comfortable majority.
Romania's external debt servicing is estimated at some $1.5 billion in 1997.
